changes: Added scribe Veṇīdatta Pāṭhaka (p3) at low confidence. His name comes only from the catalogue field; the quoted excerpt just says 'ṭīpitam idaṃ pustakaṃ' ('this book was written down') without naming anyone.
Lowered Datta (p2) to low confidence. 'vaṃśāvadaṃsadattasuta' is probably a corrupt '-vaṃśāvataṃsa-datta-suta', so the father's name may be a longer name ending in -datta.

Rewrote the place note: 'bālaya saṃjñake grāme' looks like a truncated '(devā)laya-saṃjñake grāme', which matches the catalogue's '...devālayasaṃjñake grāme'. The numbered riddle-like fragments do not make clear whether this is the copying place or the author's village.

notes: The excerpt is fragmentary. It contains numbered, riddle-like abbreviations ('sadattetyādi', 'caraketyādi', 'durgrarhagūṭhaṃ' = durgraha-gūḍham?), which suggest verses encoding names and places that the cataloguer did not quote in full. The catalogue gives the scribe as Veṇīdattapāṭhaka and the place as 'Vaijayaṃtī payovāhinī taṭinī devālayasaṃjñake grāme' (a village called Devālaya on the Vaijayantī river?). Neither appears in full in the quoted text. 'bālaya saṃjñake grāme' is probably the tail of 'devālaya-saṃjñake grāme'. The scribe is included only on the catalogue's authority. 'ṭīpitam' = 'written down / copied'. It is unclear whether the village is the copying place or the author's home. 'sadatta' might refer back to (Veṇī)datta or to the author's father Datta. No date is given.
